subject: Veridian Dedicated: sizing validation & cutover timeline
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Luke Carter <luke.carter@veridian.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: initial sizing estimate + questions

Hi Luke —

Thanks again for the time this morning. As requested, I put together an initial sizing estimate for Veridian's dedicated capacity cutover and a short list of clarifying questions so we can lock timelines and procurement items. Attached: veridian_dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx (high-level capacity calc) and a draft MAP.

High-level assumptions (please confirm):
- Target go-live window: second week of August (you mentioned Aug 9–12)
- Baseline traffic: ~50 production generation requests/second for core catalog flows, peak 120 req/s during promotions
- Average request: 1,200 input tokens, 200 generated tokens
- P50 latency SLO: 250ms (end-to-end) / P95 target: 700ms

Initial sizing (ballpark):
- Model: Redwood-13B-quant-v2 (recommended for latency/cost balance)
- Inference fleet: 12 x A100 80GB (or equivalent H100 config) configured in 6 serving nodes, continuous batching enabled
- Expected sustained throughput: ~60 req/s at p50 with ~200 token output per request (with batching + KV cache)
- Buffer for promotions/rate spikes: plan for 2x burst headroom (autoscale + reserved capacity)

Open questions for you:
1) Can you confirm the weekday/weekend traffic shape for the first 3 months?
2) Any regulatory data-residency or specific logging retention constraints beyond SOC2 (we currently offer 90-day traces by default)?
3) Procurement lead times for signing (DocuSign) and whether you need a formal PO before cutover?

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm traffic shape & PO/Docusign cadence this week
- We'll run a validation plan (described in the attachment) on a staging cluster week of Aug 4
- Tentative canary + cutover: weekend Aug 9–10 with staged traffic ramp and hosted fallback enabled

If the assumptions look off, tell me and we’ll adjust.

—
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Luke Carter <luke.carter@veridian.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: initial sizing estimate + questions

Sean — thanks for the quick turnaround and the sheet. A few clarifications:

1) Traffic shape: core catalog is pretty steady (40–60 req/s) M–F 8am–8pm PT, spikes to 100–130 req/s for 6–8 hours during promotions (normally on weekends). For the first 90 days expect a 20% ramp as we onboard.
2) Compliance: SOC2 is fine, but we require 1 year audit log retention (not 90 days). Can you support that for dedicated deployments?
3) Procurement: we can sign via DocuSign; we typically issue the PO within 2 business days after signature.

Also — our infra team asked if Redwood can provide a staging cutover runbook and an automatic rollback plan if latencies exceed SLOs. Luke C. (Procurement)

P.S. Please include the mutual action plan in the next email so we can share with Purchasing.

Folks — forwarding Veridian's clarifications. Key asks: 1yr audit-log retention, staging runbook + automated rollback, confirmation of traffic shape (they expect 20% ramp). Attached is the sizing sheet and a first draft of the MAP I built earlier.

Notes from my side after quick review of the workload and our benchmarks:
- Redwood-13B-quant-v2 is still the best mix for latency/cost at their token sizes. If Veridian is willing to accept slightly higher p95 (~800ms) we can reduce fleet size by ~15%.
- For 1-year log retention we need to confirm storage/retention tier (S3 lifecycle vs dedicated on-prem archive) — legal will need to sign off on SLA changes.

Technical ask for Markus: can you validate the attached calc and propose the minimum node count for a 2-hour outage tolerance (i.e., capacity that lets us drain and re-deploy nodes without impacting p50)? I put a rough figure 12 A100s in the sheet. Also sketch a staging test plan and rollback criteria we can send to Veridian (they want the runbook to share with their infra).

Attachments: veridian_dedicated_sizing_v1.xlsx, MAP_VERIDIAN_v2.docx

—
Sean
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Luke Carter <luke.carter@veridian.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: initial sizing estimate + questions

Sean / team — I validated the spreadsheet and sketched a concrete plan. Summary below; I also uploaded a short PNG showing p50/p95 projections for the proposed cluster.

Sizing validation (summary):
- Baseline (steady 50 req/s): 8 x A100 80GB (single-GPU inference per machine) with continuous batching and 200-token output median meets p50 ~210ms; p95 ~650–780ms depending on batch windows.
- Peak (120 req/s): reserve autoscale capacity up to 18 A100s (or 12 H100-equivalent nodes) to keep p95 < 750ms.
- Failover buffer: keep 20% headroom (hot spare capacity) in reserved pool for regional network blips.
- Draining strategy: rolling drains 1 node at a time with pre-warm cache; with 8 nodes we can tolerate a 2-node outage during maintenance without breaching p50 targets.

Staging validation & cutover timeline:
- Aug 4–6: Provision staging cluster (same config, smaller footprint) and run 48-hour soak with replayed production trace (we'll request a sampling of traffic).
- Aug 7: Run full-load validation (ramp to 120 req/s) and execute failure injection (instance reboot, network partition).
- Aug 8: Final runbook dry-run with Veridian infra; confirm 1yr retention path (Ops + Legal to sign off).
- Aug 9 (Sat) 02:00–10:00 PT: Canary cutover start — route 5% of traffic to dedicated cluster and monitor for 2 hours, then 25% for 4 hours, then 100% after a successful run.
- Aug 10 (Sun): Buffer day for rollback if issues arise. If any p95 breaches > 25% above target during ramp we will auto-fallback to Hosted API for affected routes and pause rollout.

Rollback & automation:
- Automated SLO watch: Cloudwatch/Prometheus alert if p50 or p95 crosses thresholds for >5 minutes triggers automated traffic reroute to Hosted with a human-in-loop approval required to continue.
- Runbook excerpt (paste for Veridian):
  1) Start canary at 02:00 PT, monitor metrics dashboard + error budget panel
  2) If p95 > 900ms or error rate >0.5% for 10 consecutive minutes, trigger fallback script which updates routing to Hosted endpoints and scales down dedicated pool gracefully
  3) After fallback, collect logs and create postmortem within 24h

Action items for Sales/Product:
- Sean: share staged runbook + MAP with Veridian and request a sample production trace (redacted) for our soak tests
- Monica: confirm whether 1yr audit log retention is commercially acceptable (cost delta) so we can include in the contract
- Laura: confirm customer-facing SLO wording and whether we need a formal SLA amendment for dedicated deployments

I think the Aug 9–10 window is realistic if we get their sample trace and PO by Aug 5.

-Markus
